your datapostSummarize tablepostRun aggregations over a tablepost\n\nSQL\n\nSQL querypostBatch SQL queriespost\n\n## Deleting records\n\nEdit on GitHub\n\nTo delete a record you can execute, for example:\n\nTypeScriptPythonGoSQLJSON\n\nCopy\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nconst user = await xata.db.Users.delete('rec_cd8s3r8avc42pi67m13g');\n\n// or, using the delete method on the record object:\nuser.delete();\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nCopy\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nuser = xata.records().delete(\"Users\", \"rec_cd8s3r8avc42pi67m13g\")\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nCopy\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nclient, _ := xata.NewRecordsClient()\nresponse = client.Delete(context.TODO(), xata.DeleteRecordRequest{\n  RecordRequest: xata.RecordRequest{\n    DatabaseName: xata.String(\"{db}\"),\n    TableName:    \"Users\",\n  },\n  RecordID: \"rec_cd8s3r8avc42pi67m13g\",\n})\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nCopy\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n// POST https://{workspace}.{region}.xata.sh/db/{db}:{branch}/sql\n\n{\n  \"statement\": \"DELETE FROM \\\"Users\\\" WHERE id = $1;\",\n  \"params\": [\"rec_cd8s3r8avc42pi67m13g\"]\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nCopy\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n// DELETE https://{workspace}.{region}.xata.sh/db/{db}:{branch}/tables/{table}/data/{record_id}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nIn case the record with the given ID doesn't exist, the REST API returns a 404 and the TypeScript SDK throws an exception.\n\nTransactions are used when deleting multiple records:\n\nTypeScriptPythonGoSQLJSON\n\nCopy\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nconst users = await xata.db.Users.delete(['rec_cd8s3r8avc42pi67m13g', 'rec_cgh9o1oncchhigq95n2g']);\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nCopy\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nusers = xata.records().transaction({\n  \"operations\": [\n    {\n      \"delete\": {\n        \"table\": \"Users\",\n        \"id\": \"rec_cd8s3r8avc42pi67m13g\"\n      }\n    },\n    {\n      \"delete\": {\n        \"table\": \"Users\",\n        \"id\": \"rec_cgh9o1oncchhigq95n2g\"\n      }\n    }\n  ]\n})\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nCopy\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nclient, _ := xata.NewRecordsClient()\nusers, _ := client.Transaction(context.TODO(), xata.TransactionRequest{\n  RecordRequest: xata.RecordRequest{\n    DatabaseName: xata.String(\"{db}\"),\n  },\n  Operations: []xata.TransactionOperation{\n    xata.NewDeleteTransaction(xata.TransactionDeleteOp{\n      Table: \"Users\",\n      Id:    \"rec_cd8s3r8avc42pi67m13g\",\n    }),\n    xata.NewDeleteTransaction(xata.TransactionDeleteOp{\n      Table: \"Users\",\n      Id:    \"rec_cgh9o1oncchhigq95n2g\",\n    }),\n  },\n})\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nCopy\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n// POST https://{workspace}.{region}.xata.sh/db/{db}:{branch}/sql\n\n{\n  \"statement\": \"DELETE FROM \\\"Users\\\" WHERE id IN ($1,$2);\",\n  \"params\": [\"rec_cd8s3r8avc42pi67m13g\", \"rec_cgh9o1oncchhigq95n2g\"]\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nCopy\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n// POST https://{workspace}.{region}.xata.sh/db/{db}:{branch}/transaction\n{\n  \"operations\": [\n    {\n      \"delete\": {\n        \"table\": \"Users\",\n        \"id\": \"rec_cd8s3r8avc42pi67m13g\"\n      }\n    },\n    {\n      \"delete\": {\n        \"table\": \"Users\",\n        \"id\": \"rec_cgh9o1oncchhigq95n2g\"\n      }\n    }\n  ]\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nTo delete multiple records from the API, we recommend using transactions. Transactions will not fail a delete operation if a record is not found. All operations in a transaction must succeed otherwise it is rolled back.\n\nAlternatively, you can use the &#96;DELETE&#96; statement via the SQL proxy, like in the following example:\n\nWhen dealing with a large number of records, there is a 60-second timeout. To avoid the SQL proxy's timeout, delete in small batches. We recommend limiting each deletion batch to a maximum of 10,000 records.\n\nCopy\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nDELETE FROM \"titles\"\nWHERE id IN (\n    SELECT id\n    FROM titles\n    WHERE \"originalTitle\" ILIKE '%Matrix%'\n    ORDER BY \"xata.createdAt\" ASC\n    LIMIT 10000\n);\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n* &#96;SELECT id&#96;: Specifies that only the &#96;id&#96; column will be retrieved in the query.\n* &#96;FROM titles&#96;: The subquery operates on the &#96;titles&#96; table.\n* &#96;WHERE \"originalTitle\" ILIKE '%Matrix%'&#96;: Filters rows based on a case-insensitive partial match in the &#96;originalTitle&#96; column.\n* &#96;LIMIT 10000&#96;: Restricts the number of results to a maximum of 10,000 rows.\n\n#Next Steps\n\nNow that you have seen how to do the basic create, remove, update, and delete operations, you can check out the docs on using the free text search API, which is a new super power that Xata gives you.\n\nYou can also review the pages on getting data, updating data, inserting data. We've got guides for each of these operations.",

update the content of a file item in a file array columnputDelete an item from a file arraydeleteDownload content from a file columngetUpload content to a file columnputRemove the content from a file columndelete\n\nSearch and Filter\n\nQuery tablepostFree text searchpostFree text search in a tablepostVector similarity search in a tablepostAsk your table a questionpostContinue a conversation with your datapostSummarize tablepostRun aggregations over a tablepost\n\nSQL\n\nSQL querypostBatch SQL queriespost\n\n## Creating records\n\nEdit on GitHub\n\nYou can create a record like this:\n\nTypeScriptPythonGoSQLJSON\n\nCopy\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nconst record = await xata.db.Users.create({\n  email: 'keanu@example.com',\n  name: 'Keanu Reeves'\n});\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nCopy\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nrecord = xata.records().insert(\"Users\", {\n  \"email\": \"keanu@example.com\",\n  \"name\": \"Keanu Reeves\"\n})\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nCopy\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nclient, _ := xata.NewRecordsClient()\nrecord, _ := client.Insert(context.TODO(), xata.InsertRecordRequest{\n  RecordRequest: xata.RecordRequest{\n    TableName: \"Users\",\n  },\n  Body: map[string]*xata.DataInputRecordValue{\n    \"email\": xata.ValueFromString(\"keanu@example.com\"),\n    \"name\":  xata.ValueFromString(\"Keanu Reeves\"),\n  },\n})\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nCopy\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n// POST https://{workspace}.{region}.xata.sh/db/{db}:{branch}/sql\n\n{\n  \"statement\": \"INSERT INTO \\\"Users\\\" (email,name) VALUES ($1,$2) RETURNING *;\",\n  \"params\": [\"keanu@example.com\", \"Keanu Reeves\"]\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nCopy\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n// POST https://{workspace}.{region}.xata.sh/db/{db}:{branch}/tables/{table}/data\n\n{\n  \"email\": \"keanu@example.com\",\n  \"name\": \"Keanu Reeves\"\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThe create method fails if the record ID already exists.\n\nThe SDK returns the created record and the response looks like the following:\n\nTypeScriptPythonSQLJSON\n\nCopy\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n{\n  \"email\": \"keanu@example.com\",\n  \"id\": \"rec_cd8rqcoavc42pi67lgd0\",\n  \"name\": \"Keanu Reeves\",\n  \"bio\": NULL,\n  \"address\": NULL,\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nCopy\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n{\n  \"id\": \"rec_c8hnbch26un1nl0rthkg\",\n  \"xata\": {\n    \"version\": 0,\n    \"createdAt\": \"2023-05-15T08:21:31.96526+01:00\",\n    \"updatedAt\": \"2023-05-15T21:58:54.072595+01:00\"\n  }\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nCopy\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n{\n  \"records\": [\n    {\n      \"id\": \"rec_c8hnbch26un1nl0rthkg\",\n      \"xata\": {\n        \"version\": 0,\n        \"createdAt\": \"2023-05-15T08:21:31.96526+01:00\",\n        \"updatedAt\": \"2023-05-15T08:21:31.96526+01:00\"\n      }\n    }\n  ]\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nCopy\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n{\n  \"id\": \"rec_c8hnbch26un1nl0rthkg\",\n  \"xata\": {\n    \"version\": 0,\n    \"createdAt\": \"2023-05-15T08:21:31.96526+01:00\",\n    \"updatedAt\": \"2023-05-15T21:58:54.072595+01:00\"\n  }\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nIn the above the API returns a special set of columns:\n\n* id is the ID of the record, which Xata generates automatically. The generated records are globally unique and sortable. This means that sorting by the IDs you sort by the insertion order.\n* xata.version is the version of the record. It is automatically incremented any time the record is updated and can be used for optimistic locking.\n* xata.createdAt is the timestamp when the record was created.\n* xata.updatedAt is the timestamp of last record update.\n\nIf you want to return more columns, you can specify them via the &#96;columns&#96; parameter.\n\n#Creating a record with a given ID\n\nIf you want to specify your own ID, you can do it like this:\n\nTypeScriptPythonGoSQLJSON\n\nCopy\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nconst record = await xata.db.Users.create('myid', {\n  email: 'keanu@example.com',\n  name: 'Keanu Reeves'\n});\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nCopy\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nrecord = xata.records().insert_with_id(\"Users\", \"myid\", {\n  \"email\": \"keanu@example.com\",\n  \"name\": \"Keanu Reeves\"\n})\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nCopy\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nclient, _ := xata.NewRecordsClient()\nrecord, err := client.InsertWithID(context.TODO(), xata.InsertRecordWithIDRequest{\n  RecordRequest: xata.RecordRequest{\n    TableName: \"Users\",\n  },\n  RecordID: \"myid\",\n  Body: map[string]*xata.DataInputRecordValue{\n    \"email\": xata.ValueFromString(\"keanu@example.com\"),\n    \"name\":  xata.ValueFromString(\"Keanu Reeves\"),\n  },\n})\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nCopy\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n// POST https://{workspace}.{region}.xata.sh/db/{db}:{branch}/sql\n\n{\n  \"statement\": \"INSERT INTO \\\"Users\\\" (id,email,name) VALUES ($1,$2,$3) RETURNING *;\",\n  \"params\": [\"myid\", \"keanu@example.com\", \"Keanu Reeves\"]\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nCopy\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n// PUT https://{workspace}.{region}.xata.sh/db/{db}:{branch}/tables/{table}/data/{record_id}?createOnly=true\n{\n  \"email\": \"keanu@example.com\",\n  \"name\": \"Keanu Reeves\"\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nIn the REST API example, note the change from &#96;POST&#96; to &#96;PUT&#96;. The &#96;createOnly&#96; query parameter signals Xata to return an error in case a record with the given ID already exists.\n\n#Creating a record with a linked field\n\nIn the schema that we chose, the &#96;Posts&#96; table has an &#96;author&#96; column of type &#96;link&#96; that links to the &#96;Users&#96; table. To insert a record with a linked field, use the ID of the target record in the link column.\n\nTypeScriptPythonGoSQLJSON\n\nCopy\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nconst record = await xata.db.Posts.create({\n  title: 'Filming the Matrix',\n  author: 'rec_cd8rqcoavc42pi67lgd0'\n});\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nCopy\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nrecord = xata.records().insert(\"Posts\", {\n  \"title\": \"Filming the Matrix\",\n  \"author\": \"rec_cd8rqcoavc42pi67lgd0\"\n})\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nCopy\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nclient, _ := xata.NewRecordsClient()\nrecord, _ := client.Insert(context.TODO(), xata.InsertRecordRequest{\n  RecordRequest: xata.RecordRequest{\n    TableName: \"Users\",\n  },\n  Body: map[string]*xata.DataInputRecordValue{\n    \"title\": xata.ValueFromString(\"Filming the Matrix\"),\n    \"author\":  xata.ValueFromString(\"rec_cd8rqcoavc42pi67lgd0\"),\n  },\n})\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nCopy\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n// POST https://{workspace}.{region}.xata.sh/db/{db}:{branch}/sql\n\n{\n  \"statement\": \"INSERT INTO \\\"Posts\\\" (title,author) VALUES ($1,$2) RETURNING *;\",\n  \"params\": [\"Filming the Matrix\", \"rec_cd8rqcoavc42pi67lgd0\"]\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nCopy\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n// POST https://{workspace}.{region}.xata.sh/db/{db}:{branch}/tables/{table}/data\n{\n  \"title\": \"Filming the Matrix\",\n  \"author\": \"rec_cd8rqcoavc42pi67lgd0\"\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n#Creating records in bulk\n\nIf you have multiple records to insert, you can send them in a single request via the /bulk endpoint. For example:\n\nTypeScriptPythonGoSQLJSON\n\nCopy\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nconst users = await xata.db.Users.create([\n  {\n    email: 'laurence@example.com',\n    name: 'Laurence Fishburne',\n    team: 'rec_cd8s4kbo8dsvsjilo1ug'\n  },\n  {\n    email: 'hugo@example.com',\n    name: 'Hugo Weaving',\n    team: 'rec_cd8s4kbo8dsvsjilo1ug'\n  },\n  {\n    email: 'joe@example.com',\n    name: 'Joe Pantoliano',\n    team: 'rec_cd8s4kbo8dsvsjilo1ug'\n  }\n]);\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nCopy\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nusers = xata.records().bulk_insert(\"Users\", {\n  \"records\": [\n    {\n      \"email\": \"laurence@example.com\",\n      \"name\": \"Laurence Fishburne\",\n      \"team\": \"rec_cd8s4kbo8dsvsjilo1ug\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"email\": \"hugo@example.com\",\n      \"name\": \"Hugo Weaving\",\n      \"team\": \"rec_cd8s4kbo8dsvsjilo1ug\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"email\": \"joe@example.com\",\n      \"name\": \"Joe Pantoliano\",\n      \"team\": \"rec_cd8s4kbo8dsvsjilo1ug\"\n    }\n  ]\n})\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nCopy\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nclient, _ := xata.NewRecordsClient()\nusers, _ := client.BulkInsert(context.TODO(), xata.BulkInsertRecordRequest{\n  RecordRequest: xata.RecordRequest{\n    TableName: \"Users\",\n  },\n  Columns: []string{\"name\"},\n  Records: []map[string]*xata.DataInputRecordValue{\n    {\n      \"email\": xata.ValueFromString(\"laurence@example.com\"),\n      \"name\":  xata.ValueFromString(\"Laurence Fishburne\"),\n      \"team\":  xata.ValueFromString(\"rec_cd8s4kbo8dsvsjilo1ug\"),\n    },\n    {\n      \"email\": xata.ValueFromString(\"hugo@example.com\"),\n      \"name\":  xata.ValueFromString(\"Hugo Weaving\"),\n      \"team\":  xata.ValueFromString(\"rec_cd8s4kbo8dsvsjilo1ug\"),\n    },\n    {\n      \"email\": xata.ValueFromString(\"joe@example.com\"),\n      \"name\":  xata.ValueFromString(\"Joe Pantoliano\"),\n      \"team\":  xata.ValueFromString(\"rec_cd8s4kbo8dsvsjilo1ug\"),\n    },\n  },\n})\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nCopy\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n// POST https://{workspace}.{region}.xata.sh/db/{db}:{branch}/sql\n\n{\n  \"statement\": \"INSERT INTO \\\"Users\\\" (email,name,team) VALUES ($1,$2,$3),($4,$5,$6),($7,$8,$9) RETURNING *;\",\n  \"params\": [\n    \"laurence@example.com\",\n    \"Laurence Fishburne\",\n    \"rec_cd8s4kbo8dsvsjilo1ug\",\n    \"hugo@example.com\",\n    \"Hugo Weaving\",\n    \"rec_cd8s4kbo8dsvsjilo1ug\",\n    \"joe@example.com\",\n    \"Joe Pantoliano\",\n    \"rec_cd8s4kbo8dsvsjilo1ug\"\n  ]\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nCopy\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n// POST https://{workspace}.{region}.xata.sh/db/{db}:{branch}/tables/{table}/bulk\n\n{\n  \"records\": [\n    {\n      \"email\": \"laurence@example.com\",\n      \"name\": \"Laurence Fishburne\",\n      \"team\": \"rec_cd8s4kbo8dsvsjilo1ug\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"email\": \"hugo@example.com\",\n      \"name\": \"Hugo Weaving\",\n      \"team\": \"rec_cd8s4kbo8dsvsjilo1ug\"\n    },\n    {\n      \"email\": \"joe@example.com\",\n      \"name\": \"Joe Pantoliano\",\n      \"team\": \"rec_cd8s4kbo8dsvsjilo1ug\"\n    }\n  ]\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThe bulk create method fails if the record ID already exists.\n\nIt is possible to provide IDs for each of the records. If records with the same IDs already exist, the bulk operation is canceled and an error is returned.\n\nThe &#96;file&#96; and &#96;file[]&#96; (file array) columns are not permitted in bulk requests.\n\n#Next Steps\n\nGreat! We can insert data into our databases. Let's now explore how we get data from a database. Alternatively, we can also look into updating data or deleting data. We've got guides for each of these operations.\n\n## On this page\n\nCreating a record with a given IDCreating a record with a linked fieldCreating records in bulkNext Steps",

over HTTP\n\nEdit on GitHub\n\nXata uses PostgreSQL under the hood to store your data. You can use SQL to work with your data. The results come back in a typical Xata JSON response mechanism over HTTP. If the Xata API doesn't cover the query you need, you can use SQL directly to do queries, insert data, update information, and delete records.\n\nXata offers support for a subset of PostgreSQL functions. This includes functions such as &#96;subquery&#96;, &#96;comparison&#96;, &#96;aggregate&#96;, &#96;window&#96;, &#96;range&#96;, &#96;json&#96;, &#96;string&#96;, &#96;datetime&#96;, and &#96;array&#96; functions. Functions beyond these are not permitted.\n\n#Table and column names\n\nNote when you are working with names that include upper-case letters like &#96;Users&#96; or &#96;zipCode&#96;, you must quote those otherwise PostgreSQL treats it as a lowercase name.\n\n#API Endpoint\n\n**URL:** &#96;https://{workspace}.{region}.xata.sh/db/{db}:{branch}/sql&#96;\n\n* This URL represents the endpoint for making SQL queries within the Xata platform. It's intended to enable database interaction within a designated Workspace.\n\n**Method:** &#96;POST&#96;\n\n* The HTTP method used to interact with the provided URL is &#96;POST&#96;. This means you'll be sending data to the server, specifically your SQL statement and any additional parameters.\n\n**Parameters:**\n\n* &#96;statement&#96;: Your SQL statement (required).\n* &#96;params&#96;: A list of parameters when submitting a parameterized statement.\n* &#96;consistency&#96;: This parameter refers to the level of consistency when executing a statement. It offers options such as &#96;strong&#96; and &#96;eventual&#96;. The default setting is &#96;strong&#96;.\n\n#Examples\n\nThe following are instances of working with data, including retrieving, selecting, inserting, and deleting records, using SQL in the Xata  \"xata\": {\n        \"version\": 0,\n        \"createdAt\": \"2023-05-15T08:21:31.96526+01:00\",\n        \"updatedAt\": \"2023-05-15T21:58:54.072595+01:00\"\n      }\n    }\n  ]\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n#Select a subset of columns from your table\n\nTypeScriptPythonJSON\n\nCopy\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nconst { records } = await xata.sql\u003cTeamsRecord\u003e&#96;SELECT name, city (name, email) VALUES ($1, $2)\",\n  [name, email]\n)\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nCopy\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n// POST https://{workspace}.{region}.xata.sh/db/{db}:{branch}/sql\n\n{\n  \"statement\": \"INSERT INTO \"statement\": \"SELECT * FROM \\\"Users\\\" LIMIT 10;\",\n  \"consistency\": \"eventual\"\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n#Limitations\n\nWhen using SQL in Xata, there are a few constraints to keep in mind.\n\n#Data retrieval\n\n* The &#96;xata.*&#96; internal fields are read-only. You cannot modify these fields.\n* You can only submit one statement per request.\n* Xata returns 1000 records at a time. Access your data using &#96;LIMIT&#96; and &#96;OFFSET&#96; to iterate and work through your data.\n* JSON formatter functions do not work as the endpoint already returns a JSON response.\n* The &#96;work_mem&#96; setting in PostgreSQL is set to 4 MB. so a query can use only 4 MB of memory (before writing to temp files)\n\n#Resource consumption\n\n* In PostgreSQL, the &#96;work_mem&#96; configuration is set to 4 MB. A query is limited to 4 MB of memory and this limit is enforced before the data is saved into temporary files. The &#96;work_mem&#96; configuration sets the baseline maximum memory for query operations like sorting or using hash tables before writing to temporary disk file.\n* The &#96;hash_mem_multiplier&#96; is set to &#96;1&#96;. The &#96;hash_mem_multiplier&#96; computes the maximum memory for hash-based operations by multiplying it by &#96;work_mem&#96;. For additional information on resource consumption in Postgres, see the PostgreSQL docs.\n\n#Column names\n\nColumns with matching names overwrite each other by default. To address this, especially when dealing with multiple columns that have the same name, you can use column aliasing as a solution. For instance:\n\nCopy\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nSELECT address AS physical_address, address AS email\nFROM people, emails\nWHERE people.id=emails.id;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nBy assigning aliases, you can distinguish between columns with similar names and manage them effectively.\n\n#Supported commands\n\nXata supports the following essential Data Manipulation Language (DML) SQL commands, which are fundamental for managing and manipulating data within database tables:\n\n* &#96;SELECT&#96;: This command is used to retrieve data from a database. It allows you to select one or more columns of a table, with various options for filtering, sorting, and grouping the data.\n* &#96;INSERT&#96;: This command is used to add new records (rows) to a table. It specifies the table to insert into and the values for the new row.\n* &#96;DELETE&#96;: This command removes existing records from a table. It can be used with conditions to specify which records should be deleted.\n* &#96;UPDATE&#96;: This command modifies existing records in a table such as correcting errors or updating information. Like DELETE, it can be used with conditions to specify which records should be updated and how.\n\nPlease refer to the supported commands table to get a full break down.\n\n#Unsupported commands\n\nThe following table provides examples of commands that are currently **not supported** in Xata:\n\n| Command type                           | Description                                             | Unsupported commands                                                |\n| -------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n| **Data Definition Language (DDL)**     | Used for defining or altering database structures       | CREATE, DROP, ALTER, TRUNCATE                                       |\n| **Data Manipulation Language (DML)**   | Typically used for data manipulation                    | UPSERT, SEQUENCE                                                    |\n| **Data Control Language (DCL)**        | Manages user permissions and access control             | GRANT, REVOKE                                                       |\n| **Transaction Control Language (TCL)** | Crucial for managing the state of database transactions | COMMIT, ROLLBACK, SAVEPOINT, ROLLBACK TO SAVEPOINT, SET TRANSACTION |\n\n#Connection methods\n\nSQL access in Xata is achieved via an HTTP or HTTPS proxy. Tools that use a wire protocol with a connection string to PostgreSQL are not compatible with Xata's SQL proxy.\n\nYou can use SQL in Xata with any of the following methods:\n\n* Use the built-in PostgreSQL Playground in the Xata Web UI.\n* Execute API calls to your branch's &#96;/sql&#96; endpoint using web clients such as Postman.\n* Use the SQL methods provided in the Typescript and Python SDKs.\n* Use the Kysely and Drizzle integrations.\n\n## On this page\n\nTable and column namesAPI EndpointExamplesFetch all recordsSelect a subset of columns from your tableInsert a new record using a parameterized queryDelete record using a parameterized queryQuery records from the replica storeLimitationsData retrievalResource consumptionColumn namesSupported commandsUnsupported commandsConnection methods",

SDK for Python\n\nEdit on GitHub\n\nThis feature is deprecated and no longer recommended for use in new applications. It will continue to be maintained, but no further enhancements are planned.\n\nThe Python SDK is available as a PyPI package. It uses type annotations and requires Python 3.8 or higher. The API reference is located at \u003chttps://xata-py.readthedocs.io\u003e.\n\n#Installation\n\nTo install the library enter the following command:\n\nCopy\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\npip install xata\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThe &#96;xata&#96; package is a standalone SDK library that features &#96;XataClient&#96;. By installing the package, you can import the SDK into your Python project and start building on top of Xata.\n\nThe Python SDK is different from the Xata CLI which can be used to manage your Xata databases from the command line or import the Typescript and Javascript client.\n\n#Configuration\n\n#Workspace URL\n\nTo bootstrap the SDK we recommend you use the workspace URL. In the Web UI, navigate to **Workspaces** then **Configuration**. You will be directed to the workspace API base URL. Copy the URL and use it to configure routing.\n\nThe URL can be passed to the client as a parameter:\n\nCopy\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nxata = XataClient(db_url=\"REDACTED_DB_URL\")\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nOr you can set the environment variable: &#96;XATA_DATABASE_URL&#96;. The parameter value will take precedence over the environment variable.\n\nThe format of the database URL (&#96;db_url&#96;) parameter must follow the format of: &#96;https://test-123456.us-east-1.xata.sh/db/mydb&#96;. The branch name is not mandatory, it can be either appended to the URL, with a &#96;:&#96; as the separator, like this &#96;https://test-123456.us-east-1.xata.sh/db/mydb:my-feature-branch&#96;. Alternatively, you can specify the &#96;branch_name&#96; with the parameter in &#96;XataClient&#96;.\n\n#Authorization\n\nThere are multiple options to pass your Xata credentials to the client. Xata will check the following using this order of precedence:\n\n1. Parameters passed to the constructor\n2. Environment variables\n3. The &#96;.env&#96; file\n4. Via &#96;.xatarc&#96; configuration file\n\nThe &#96;.xatarc&#96; file is generated by the Xata CLI in the current directory when running the command &#96;xata init&#96;.\n\n\u003c#dotenv\u003e\n\nIf the previous options were empty, the client looks for a &#96;.env&#96; file in the project root directory. Visit the Authentication page to read more about best practices.\n\nCopy\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nXATA_API_KEY=\"REDACTED_API_KEY\"\nXATA_DATABASE_URL=\"REDACTED_DB_URL\"\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n#xatarc configuration file\n\nThe &#96;.xatarc&#96; configuration file is the final source to retrieve the API key and the workspace. Refer to the authentication page to learn more about the &#96;.xatarc&#96; file and best practices.\n\n#Environment Variables\n\nIf no parameters passed, the client probes the following environment variables for authentication.\n\nCopy\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nexport XATA_API_KEY=\"REDACTED_API_KEY\"\nexport XATA_DATABASE_URL=\"REDACTED_DB_URL\"\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nCopy\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nfrom xata.client import XataClient\n\nclient = XataClient()\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n#Parameters\n\nInject the API key and workspace &#96;id&#96; directly into the constructor as a parameter:\n\nCopy\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nfrom xata.client import XataClient\n\nclient = XataClient(api_key=\"REDACTED_API_KEY\", db_url=\"REDACTED_DB_URL\")\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n#Selecting a Branch\n\nThere are multiple options to point the SDK to a specific branch, if none is selected, the SDK elects &#96;main&#96; as current branch name.\n\nThe environment variable &#96;XATA_BRANCH&#96; can specify a branch, the SDK will look for the variable and initialize the SDK with that value.\n\nYou can also, set the branch with the database URL (&#96;db_url&#96;) on SDK init, we want to use the branch &#96;feature-042&#96; on the database &#96;Planes&#96;, we can initialize the SDK with:\n\nCopy\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nxata = XataClient(db_url=\"https://test-12345.us-east-1.xata.sh/db/Planes:feature-042\")\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nAnother options is to specify the &#96;branch_name&#96; in the SDK. If you specify &#96;db_url&#96; and &#96;branch_name&#96;, the latter will be ignored.\n\nIf you want to change the branch for a single request, you can do so with all workspace endpoints, by setting the &#96;branch_name&#96;:\n\nCopy\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nxata.records().insert(\"Planes\", record, branch_name=\"feature-042\")\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n#API Namespace\n\nThe API surface of the Python SDK is organized into namespaces, with each namespace associated with a specific set of APIs. For instance, the &#96;databases&#96; namespace provides access to all the available Xata endpoints for managing databases.\n\nAlternatively, you can directly instantiate a namespace, as demonstrated in this example.\n\n| Authentication and API key management                            | client.authentication() |\n| ---------------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------- |\n| Branch management                                                | client.branch()         |\n| Database operations                                              | client.databases()      |\n| User invites management                                          | client.invites()        |\n| Branch schema migrations and history                             | client.migrations()     |\n| User management                                                  | client.users()          |\n| Workspace management                                             | client.workspaces()     |\n| Table records access operations                                  | client.records()        |\n| APIs for searching, querying, filtering, and aggregating records | client.data()           |\n| Database table management                                        | client.table()          |\n| SQL over HTTP                                                    | client.sql()            |\n\nThe endpoints and namespaces are generated from the OpenAPI specification.\n\n#Examples\n\nThe following examples assume the &#96;client&#96; variable is an instance of &#96;XataClient&#96; with the correct credentials. To learn more about initializing the SDK, refer to the Configuration page.\n\nEach endpoint returns an instance of requests.Response. If your query reaches the threshold of concurrent connections, the server will respond with a &#96;429&#96; status code and the SDK will throw a RateLimitingException.\n\nYou can refer to the API Reference for the relevant parameters to each method.\n\nMore examples are available in the GitHub repository of the SDK, including runnable demo apps for the BulkProcessor, pagination of query results, and leveraging transactions.\n\n#At a glance\n\nBelow are the parameters passed to the methods in the following examples:\n\n* &#96;xata.records().insert()&#96;: table name (str), record (dictionary)\n* &#96;xata.records().insert_with_id()&#96;: table name (str), record id (str), record (dictionary)\n* &#96;xata.records().update()&#96;: table name (str), record id (str), record (dictionary)\n* &#96;xata.records().upsert()&#96;: table name (str), record id (str), record (dictionary)\n* &#96;xata.records().get()&#96;: table name (str), record id (str)\n* &#96;xata.records().bulk_insert()&#96;: table name (str), records (dictionary with records array)\n* &#96;xata.users().get()&#96;\n* &#96;xata.data().ask()&#96;: table name (str), question (str)\n* &#96;xata.data().ask_follow_up()&#96;: table name (str), session id (str), question (str)\n* &#96;to_rfc3339()&#96;: dt (datetime), tz (timezone, default: utc)\n* &#96;xata.table().create()&#96;: table name (str)\n* &#96;xata.table().set_schema()&#96;: table name (str), table schema (dictionary)\n\n#Insert or update a new record\n\n1.x0.x\n\nCopy\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nfrom xata.client import XataClient\n\nxata = XataClient(db_name=\"my_db\")\n\nrecord = {\n  \"name\": \"Peter Parker\",\n  \"job\": \"Spiderman\",\n}\n\n# Insert record to table \"Avengers\" and let Xata generate a record Id\n\nresp = xata.records().insert(\"Avengers\", record)\nassert resp.is_success()\nprint(\"Record Id: %s\" % resp[\"id\"])\n\n# Insert record to table \"Avengers\" with your own record Id \"spidey-1\"\n\nresp = xata.records().insert_with_id(\"Avengers\", \"spidey-1\", record)\nassert resp.is_success()\n\n# Update the record with Id \"spidey-1\" in table \"Avengers\"\n\nrecord[\"job\"] = \"your friendly neighborhood spider man\"\nresp = xata.records().update(\"Avengers\", \"spidey-1\", record)\nassert resp.is_success()\n\n# Upsert: Update or insert a record\n\nrecord = {\n  \"name\": \"Bruce Banner\",\n  \"job\": \"Hulk\",\n}\nresp = xata.records().upsert(\"Avengers\", \"hulk-1\", record)\n\n# On insert status code = 201\n\nassert resp.status_code == 201\nassert resp.is_success()\n\nrecord[\"job\"] = \"the incredible hulk\"\nresp = xata.records().upsert(\"Avengers\", \"spidey-1\", record)\n\n# On update status code = 200\n\nassert resp.status_code == 200\nassert resp.is_success()\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nCopy\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nfrom xata.client import XataClient\n\nclient = XataClient(db_name=\"my_db\")\n\nrecord = {\n  \"name\": \"Peter Parker\",\n  \"job\": \"Spiderman\",\n}\n\n# Insert record to table \"Avengers\" and let Xata generate a record ID\nresp = client.records().insertRecord(\"Avengers\", record)\nassert resp.status_code == True\n\nprint(spiderman)\n\n# {\"id\": \"spidey\", \"name\": \"Peter Parker\", \"job\": \"spiderman\"}\n\n# If the record with the Id does not exist, the status code will be 404\n\nbatman = records.get(\"Avengers\", \"bruce-wayne\")\nprint(batman.status_code) # 404\nprint(batman.is_success()) # False\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nCopy\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nfrom xata.client import XataClient\nrecords = XataClient().records()\n\nspiderman = records.getRecord(\"Avengers\", \"spidey\")\nprint(spiderman.json())\n# {\"id\": \"spidey\", \"name\": \"Peter Parker\", \"job\": \"spiderman\"}\n\n# If the record with the Id does not exist, the status code will be 404\nbatman = records.getRecord(\"Avengers\", \"bruce-wayne\")\nprint(batman.status_code)\n# 404\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n#Query records from a table (using server-side filters and sorts)\n\nThe following example shows how to query a table and apply filters and sorts. We will query the table &#96;Avengers&#96;, and apply some filters.\n\n1.x0.x\n\nCopy\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nfrom xata.client import XataClient\n\nresp = xata.data().query(\"Avengers\", {\n  \"columns\": [\"name\", \"thumbnail\"], # the columns we want returned\n  \"filter\": { \"job\": \"spiderman\" }, # optional filters to apply\n  \"sort\": { \"name\": \"desc\" }        # optional sorting key and order (asc/desc)\n})\nassert resp.is_success()\n\nprint(resp[\"records\"])\n# [{\"id\": \"spidey\", \"name\": \"Peter Parker\", \"job\": \"spiderman\"}]\n# Note it will be an array, even if there is only one record matching the filters\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nCopy\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nfrom xata.client import XataClient\n\nresp = xata.search_and_filter().queryTable(\"Avengers\", {\n  \"columns\": [\"name\", \"thumbnail\"], # the columns we want returned\n  \"filter\": { \"job\": \"spiderman\" }, # optional filters to apply\n  \"sort\": { \"name\": \"desc\" }        # optional sorting key and order (asc/desc)\n})\n# queryTable returns status code = 200\nassert resp.status_code == 200\n\nrecords = resp.json()\nprint(data[\"records\"])\n# [{\"id\": \"spidey\", \"name\": \"Peter Parker\", \"job\": \"spiderman\"}]\n# Note it will be an array, even if there is only one record matching the filters\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n#Pagination\n\nThe following example will show you how to paginate through your data, and introduce you to two new convenience methods, &#96;response.has_more_results()&#96; and &#96;response.get_cursor()&#96; introduced in &#96;1.x&#96;. We want to limit the records per call to 25, and assume the &#96;people&#96; table has a total amount of records is \u003e 25\\. So we need to make multiple calls to page through our data.\n\n1.x0.x\n\nCopy\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nfrom xata.client import XataClient\n\nxata = XataClient()\n\nrecords = xata.data().query(\"people\", {\n  \"page\": {\n    \"size\": 25 # limit result set to 25 records\n  }\n})\n\n# do something with the data ..\n\n# are more pages available ? If yes keep looping\n# through until we reached the last page\nwhile records.has_more_results():\n  # fetch the next page ...\n  records = xata.data().query(\"people\", {\n    \"page\": {\n      \"after\": records.get_cursor() # get the next cursor\n    }\n  })\n  # do something with the data ..\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nCopy\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nfrom xata.client import XataClient\n\nxata = XataClient()\n\nrecords = xata.data().queryTable(\"people\", {\n  \"page\": {\n    \"size\": 25 # limit result set to 25 records\n  }\n})\n# do something with the data ...\n\n# are more pages available ? If yes keep looping\n# through until we reached the last page\nmore = records.json()[\"meta\"][\"page\"][\"more\"]\nwhile more:\n  # fetch the next page ..\n  records = xata.data().query(\"people\", {\n    \"page\": {\n      \"after\": records..json()[\"meta\"][\"page\"][\"cursor\"] # next cursor\n    }\n  })\n  # do something with the data ..\n  more = records.json()[\"meta\"][\"page\"][\"more\"]\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n#Delete a record from a table\n\n1.x0.x\n\nCopy\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nfrom xata.client import XataClient\nrecords = XataClient().records()\n\nrecord = records.delete(\"Avengers\", \"captain-america\")\nprint(record.status_code) # 204\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nCopy\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nfrom xata.client import XataClient\nrecords = XataClient().records()\n\nrecord = records.deleteRecord(\"Avengers\", \"captain-america\")\nprint(record.status_code) # 204\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n#Insert records in bulk\n\nThe Bulk Processor is a helpful tool for performing bulk operations using the Xata Python client. It abstracts away the complexity of managing bulk operations, making it easier to perform large-scale insert operations. Using the Bulk Processor is recommended for bulk operations in Xata.\n\n1.x0.x\n\nCopy\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nfrom xata.client import XataClient\n\nxata = XataClient(api_key=\"REDACTED_API_KEY\", db_name=\"my_db\", branch_name=\"feature-042\")\n\navengers = [\n  {\"name\": \"Peter Parker\", \"job\": \"Spiderman\"},\n  {\"name\": \"Bruce Banner\", \"job\": \"Hulk\"},\n  {\"name\": \"Steve Rodgers Parker\", \"job\": \"Captain America\"},\n  {\"name\": \"Tony Stark\", \"job\": \"Iron Man\"},\n]\nresp = xata.records().bulk_insert(\"Avengers\", {\"records\": avengers})\nassert resp.is_success()\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nCopy\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nfrom xata.client import XataClient\n\nclient = XataClient(api_key=\"REDACTED_API_KEY\", db_name=\"my_db\", branch_name=\"feature-042\")\n\navengers = [\n  {\"name\": \"Peter Parker\", \"job\": \"Spiderman\"},\n  {\"name\": \"Bruce Banner\", \"job\": \"Hulk\"},\n  {\"name\": \"Steve Rodgers Parker\", \"job\": \"Captain America\"},\n  {\"name\": \"Tony Stark\", \"job\": \"Iron Man\"},\n]\nresp = client.records().bulkInsertTableRecords(\"Avengers\", {\"records\": avengers})\nassert resp.status_code == 200\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n#Upload a file\n\nIn this scenario we are uploading an on disk hosted file into a table &#96;Photos&#96; through the records API. For more examples please consult the file attachment examples.\n\n1.x0.x\n\nCopy\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nxata = XataClient()\n\nupload = xata.records().insert(\"Photos\", {\n  \"title\": \"My new uploaded photo\",\n  \"photo\": {\n    \"name\": \"Nordkette, Innsbruck\",\n    \"mediaType\": \"image/jpeg\",\n    \"base64Content\": \"Tm9yZGtldHRlLCBJbm5zYnJ1Y2ssIFR5cm9sLCBBdXN0cmlhLCBMb3JlbSBJcHN1bSBsb3Jv\",\n    \"enablePublicUrl\": True\n  }\n})\nassert upload.is_success()\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nCopy\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nxata = XataClient()\n\nupload = xata.records().insertRecord(\"Photos\", {\n  \"title\": \"My new uploaded photo\",\n  \"photo\": {\n    \"name\": \"Nordkette, Innsbruck\",\n    \"mediaType\": \"image/jpeg\",\n    \"base64Content\": \"Tm9yZGtldHRlLCBJbm5zYnJ1Y2ssIFR5cm9sLCBBdXN0cmlhLCBMb3JlbSBJcHN1bSBsb3Jv\",\n    \"enablePublicUrl\": True\n  }\n})\nassert upload.status_code == 201\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nThe following snippets shows you a very simple way to read a file from disk and encode it to base 64:\n\nCopy\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nfile_name = \"photos/nordkette.jpg\"\nwith open(file_name, \"rb\") as f:\n  file_content = f.read()\nb64 = base64.b64encode(file_content).decode(\"ascii\")\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n#Ask AI Endpoint with follow up\n\nThe &#96;ask&#96; endpoint uses search or similarity search algorithms to find relevant information from your database. Please refer to this page to get more information about the endpoint.\n\n1.x0.x\n\nCopy\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nxata = XataClient()\n\nanswer = xata.data().ask(\"xata\", \"does xata have a python sdk\")\nassert answer.is_success()\n\nprint(\"Answer : %s\" % answer[\"answer\"])\nprint(\"Records: %s\" % answer[\"records\"])\nprint(\"Session: %s\" % answer[\"sessionId\"])\n\n# Ask a follow up question using the sessionId from the previous question\n\nfollow_up = xata.data().ask_follow_up(\"xata\", answer[\"sessionId\"], \"what is the best way to do bulk?\")\nassert follow_up.is_success()\n\nprint(\"Answer : %s\" % follow_up[\"answer\"])\nprint(\"Records: %s\" % follow_up[\"records\"])\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nCopy\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nclient = XataClient(api_key=\"REDACTED_API_KEY\", workspace_id=\"REDACTED_WS_ID\")\nclient.set_db_and_branch_names(\"harry-potter\", \"main\")\n\nquestion_to_ask = \"is harry potter able to fly?\"\nresp = client.search_and_filter().askTable(my_table_name, {\n  \"question\": question_to_ask\n})\n\nassert resp.status_code == 200\nprint(\"Answer : %s\" % resp.json()[\"answer\"])\nprint(\"Records: %s\" % resp.json()[\"records\"])\n\n# [!] follow up questions only available in 1.x version of the SDK\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n#Get the current User\n\n1.x0.x\n\nCopy\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nfrom xata.client import XataClient\n\nxata = XataClient()\n\nuser = xata.users().get()\nprint(user.status_code) # 200\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nCopy\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nfrom xata.client import XataClient\n\nclient = XataClient()\n\nuser = client.users().getUser()\nprint(user.status_code) # 200\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n#Handling RFC 3339 dates\n\nTo use the datetime data type in Xata, you must provide an RFC 3339 compliant string.\n\nThe Xata SDK provides a convenient &#96;to_rfc3339()&#96; helper function to simplify the submission of Python native datetime values. You can pass the &#96;datetime&#96; object as a parameter to the helper function, and it will convert the value to a RFC 3339 compliant string.\n\nTo specify a timezone, you can do so by using the optional &#96;timezone&#96; argument. If no timezone is specified, UTC time is applied by default.\n\nThe &#96;to_rfc3339()&#96; helper function was introduced with the v0.9.0 release.\n\nCopy\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n# import the helper function\nfrom xata.helpers import to_rfc339\nfrom datetime import datetime\n\n#\nmy_date = datetime.strptime(\"2023-03-20 13:42:00\", \"%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S\")\nprint(to_rfc339(my_date))\n\u003e \"2023-03-20T13:42:00+00:00\"\n\n# with time\ndate_without_time = datetime.strptime(\"2023-03-20\", \"%Y-%m-%d\")\nprint(to_rfc339(date_without_time))\n\u003e \"2023-03-20T00:00:00+00:00\"\n\n# With a timezone\nfrom pytz import timezone\n\ndate_with_tz = datetime.strptime(\"2023-03-20 13:42:16\", \"%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S\")\ntz_europe_vienna = timezone(\"Europe/Vienna\")\nprint(to_rfc339(date_with_tz, tz_europe_vienna))\n\u003e \"2023-03-20T13:42:16+01:05\"\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n#Updating the table schema\n\nThe Xata SDK provides schema editing operations under the Table class.\n\nYou can create tables, add and delete columns, or set the full table schema.\n\nCopy\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nfrom xata.client import XataClient\nxata = XataClient()\n\ntable_schema = {\n  \"columns\": [\n    {\n      \"name\": \"title\",\n      \"type\": \"string\",\n    },\n    {\n      \"name\": \"description\",\n      \"type\": \"text\",\n      \"notNull\": True,\n      \"defaultValue\": \"Default text\"\n    }\n  ]\n}\n\nassert xata.table().create(\"mytable\").is_success()\n\nresp = xata.table().set_schema(\"mytable\", table_schema)\n\n# if the operation failed, print the server response\nassert resp.is_success(), resp\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n#Bulk Processor\n\nIf you want to ingest multiple records in Xata, using &#96;bulk&#96; is the most efficient way. The &#96;BulkProcessor&#96;, a helper of the Python SDK, aims to make the process even simpler by abstracting away any complexity of juggling concurrent workers or chunking data, or maintaining queues.\n\nYou can use the &#96;BulkProcessor&#96; to e.g. ingest a CSV file into Xata or read documents from a queue and delegate the ingestion to the processor.\n\nTwo methods are available to put data in the processing queue:\n\n* &#96;bp.put_records(\":table\", \":records\")&#96; to add multiple records\n* &#96;bp.put_record(\":table\", \":record\")&#96; to add only one record\n\nUsing the option of multiples, &#96;bp.add_records(\":table\", \":records\")&#96; is more efficient as it requires less locking of the internal data structures.\n\n#Configuration Options\n\nYou can tweak the processor to your needs if necessary:\n\n* &#96;thread_pool_size&#96;: How many data queue workers should be deployed (default: 4)\n* &#96;batch_size&#96;: How many records per table should be pushed as batch (default: 25)\n* &#96;flush_interval&#96;: After how many seconds should the per table queue be flushed (default: 5 seconds)\n* &#96;processing_timeout&#96;: Cooldown period between batches (default: 0.025 seconds)\n\nIf data is coming slowly, e.g. \u003e 1 record / second, it's reasonable to have fewer threads deployed and decrease the &#96;batch_size&#96; and &#96;flush_interval&#96; to get documents in faster.\n\n#How to ingest many records\n\nCopy\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nfrom xata.client import XataClient\nfrom xata.helpers import BulkProcessor\n\nclient = XataClient()\nbp = BulkProcessor(client)\n\n# The dict keys match the columns in the destination table \"Users\"\ndata = [\n   {\"name\": \"Max Musterman\", \"email\": \"max@acme.co\"},\n   {\"name\": \"Ida von Klammer\", \"email\": \"ida@acme.co\"},\n   # ... more records\n   {\"name\": \"Mia Diaz\", \"email\": \"mia@acme.co\"},\n]\n# Add records to processor\nbp.put_records(\"Users\", data)\n# Ensure the Processing queue is flushed before the script terminates.\n# This command will halt the script until all records have been pushed.\nbp.flush_queue()\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n#How to ingest data from a queue\n\nCopy\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nfrom xata.client import XataClient\nfrom xata.helpers import BulkProcessor\n\nclient = XataClient()\nbp = BulkProcessor(client)\n\n# Sub to a queue and continuously read messages\nwhile queue.subscribed():\n   msg = queue.read()\n\n   # Reading destination and data from queue\n   table_name = msg[\"table\"]\n   record = msg[\"data\"]\n\n   # Add records to processor\n   bp.put_record(table_name, record)\n\n# Ensure the Processing queue is flushed before the script terminates.\n# This command will halt the script until all records have been pushed.\nbp.flush_queue()\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n#Logging\n\nThe SDK builds on the requests package and includes built-in logging support. By configuring the log level to debug, you can view the URL and status code by default. The &#96;BulkProcessor&#96; just like the client use the &#96;logging&#96; package and will emit logs.\n\n#Migrating from 0.x to 1.x\n\nIf you are currently a user of a &#96;0.x&#96; version of the Python SDK, and intend to upgrade the SDK version to &#96;1.x&#96;, please consider the following breaking changes. We documented all changes to promoted the SDK to GA in the ticket xataio/xata-py#24.\n\n#New API Response type\n\nStatus: &#96;future breaking&#96; xataio/xata-py#101\n\nThe response of an API used to of type &#96;requests.Response&#96;, this changed in favour of a custom class called ApiResponse. This class inherits the build in &#96;dict&#96; data type and hence allows to drop the previously needed &#96;.json()&#96; method to get access to data. The method &#96;.json()&#96; is still available, for a non-breaking upgrade, but pronounced deprecated and will be removed with the next major release. The properties &#96;status_code&#96; and &#96;headers&#96; are replicated. For further convenience you don't need to check the status code anymore, you can simply use the method &#96;is_success()&#96; to check if the request was successful.\n\nIn &#96;0.x&#96; getting a record required the &#96;.json()&#96; to access the data.\n\nCopy\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\npost = xata.records().getRecord(\"Posts\", \"12345\")\nprint(post.json()) # {\"record\": {\"id\": \"12345\", \"title\": \"a blog post\"}}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nIn &#96;1.0.0&#96; the response is implied to be a &#96;dict&#96; and ready to be used.\n\nCopy\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\npost = xata.records().get(\"Posts\", \"12345\")\nprint(post) # {\"record\": {\"id\": \"12345\", \"title\": \"a blog post\"}}\n\n# alternatively, the legacy way using .json()\npost = xata.records().get(\"Posts\", \"12345\")\nprint(post.json()) # {\"record\": {\"id\": \"12345\", \"title\": \"a blog post\"}}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n#Change of API surface\n\nStatus: &#96;breaking&#96; xataio/xata-py#93\n\nThe API surface was clunky with duplicate names, creating long function calls and did not comply with pep-8 function names.\n\nListing all databases in &#96;0.x&#96;\n\nCopy\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nlst = xata.databases().getDatabaseList()\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nchanged to a more concise call in &#96;1.x&#96;:\n\nCopy\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nlst = xata.databases().list()\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nContinuously the function arguments are also converted to the pep-8 standard, lowercased and separated by an underscore, &#96;SessionId&#96; becomes &#96;session_id&#96;.\n\n#Error Handling\n\n#Renamed Exceptions\n\nStatus: &#96;breaking&#96;\n\nIn order to align with the pep-8 standard that defines the naming to exceptions, the following classes were renamed:\n\n* &#96;UnauthorizedException&#96; to &#96;UnauthorizedError&#96;\n* &#96;RateLimitException&#96; to &#96;RateLimitError&#96;\n* &#96;ServerErrorException&#96; to &#96;XataServerError&#96;\n\n#Throwing errors on failed requests\n\nIf a requests results in a HTTP status code not in the &#96;2xx&#96; range, an error will be raised. The errors depend on the status code:\n\n* &#96;401&#96;: &#96;UnauthorizedError&#96;\n* &#96;429&#96;: &#96;RateLimitError&#96;\n* &#96;500&#96;: &#96;XataServerError&#96;\n\n#Removed deprecated methods\n\nStatus: &#96;breaking&#96; xataio/xata-py#17\n\nThe following methods were pronounced deprecated with the &#96;0.7.0&#96; release of the SDK and were removed with the &#96;1.0.0&#96; major version:\n\n* &#96;client.get()&#96;\n* &#96;client.post()&#96;\n* &#96;client.put()&#96;\n* &#96;client.patch()&#96;\n* &#96;client.delete()&#96;\n* &#96;client.request()&#96;\n\n## On this page\n\nInstallationConfigurationWorkspace URLAuthorizationdotenvxatarc configuration fileEnvironment VariablesParametersSelecting a BranchAPI NamespaceExamplesAt a glanceInsert or update a new recordGet a record from a tableQuery records from a table (using server-side filters and sorts)PaginationDelete a record from a tableInsert records in bulkUpload a fileAsk AI Endpoint with follow upGet the current UserHandling RFC 3339 datesUpdating the table schemaBulk ProcessorConfiguration OptionsHow to ingest many recordsHow to ingest data from a queueLoggingMigrating from 0.x to 1.xNew API Response typeChange of API surfaceError HandlingRenamed ExceptionsThrowing errors on failed requestsRemoved deprecated methods",

your datapostSummarize tablepostRun aggregations over a tablepost\n\nSQL\n\nSQL querypostBatch SQL queriespost\n\n## Deleting records\n\nEdit on GitHub\n\nTo delete a record you can execute, for example:\n\nTypeScriptPythonGoSQLJSON\n\nCopy\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nconst user = await xata.db.Users.delete('rec_cd8s3r8avc42pi67m13g');\n\n// or, using the delete method on the record object:\nuser.delete();\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nCopy\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nuser = xata.records().delete(\"Users\", \"rec_cd8s3r8avc42pi67m13g\")\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nCopy\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nclient, _ := xata.NewRecordsClient()\nresponse = client.Delete(context.TODO(), xata.DeleteRecordRequest{\n  RecordRequest: xata.RecordRequest{\n    DatabaseName: xata.String(\"{db}\"),\n    TableName:    \"Users\",\n  },\n  RecordID: \"rec_cd8s3r8avc42pi67m13g\",\n})\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nCopy\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n// POST https://{workspace}.{region}.xata.sh/db/{db}:{branch}/sql\n\n{\n  \"statement\": \"DELETE FROM \\\"Users\\\" WHERE id = $1;\",\n  \"params\": [\"rec_cd8s3r8avc42pi67m13g\"]\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nCopy\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n// DELETE https://{workspace}.{region}.xata.sh/db/{db}:{branch}/tables/{table}/data/{record_id}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nIn case the record with the given ID doesn't exist, the REST API returns a 404 and the TypeScript SDK throws an exception.\n\nTransactions are used when deleting multiple records:\n\nTypeScriptPythonGoSQLJSON\n\nCopy\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nconst users = await xata.db.Users.delete(['rec_cd8s3r8avc42pi67m13g', 'rec_cgh9o1oncchhigq95n2g']);\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nCopy\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nusers = xata.records().transaction({\n  \"operations\": [\n    {\n      \"delete\": {\n        \"table\": \"Users\",\n        \"id\": \"rec_cd8s3r8avc42pi67m13g\"\n      }\n    },\n    {\n      \"delete\": {\n        \"table\": \"Users\",\n        \"id\": \"rec_cgh9o1oncchhigq95n2g\"\n      }\n    }\n  ]\n})\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nCopy\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nclient, _ := xata.NewRecordsClient()\nusers, _ := client.Transaction(context.TODO(), xata.TransactionRequest{\n  RecordRequest: xata.RecordRequest{\n    DatabaseName: xata.String(\"{db}\"),\n  },\n  Operations: []xata.TransactionOperation{\n    xata.NewDeleteTransaction(xata.TransactionDeleteOp{\n      Table: \"Users\",\n      Id:    \"rec_cd8s3r8avc42pi67m13g\",\n    }),\n    xata.NewDeleteTransaction(xata.TransactionDeleteOp{\n      Table: \"Users\",\n      Id:    \"rec_cgh9o1oncchhigq95n2g\",\n    }),\n  },\n})\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nCopy\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n// POST https://{workspace}.{region}.xata.sh/db/{db}:{branch}/sql\n\n{\n  \"statement\": \"DELETE FROM \\\"Users\\\" WHERE id IN ($1,$2);\",\n  \"params\": [\"rec_cd8s3r8avc42pi67m13g\", \"rec_cgh9o1oncchhigq95n2g\"]\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nCopy\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n// POST https://{workspace}.{region}.xata.sh/db/{db}:{branch}/transaction\n{\n  \"operations\": [\n    {\n      \"delete\": {\n        \"table\": \"Users\",\n        \"id\": \"rec_cd8s3r8avc42pi67m13g\"\n      }\n    },\n    {\n      \"delete\": {\n        \"table\": \"Users\",\n        \"id\": \"rec_cgh9o1oncchhigq95n2g\"\n      }\n    }\n  ]\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nTo delete multiple records from the API, we recommend using transactions. Transactions will not fail a delete operation if a record is not found. All operations in a transaction must succeed otherwise it is rolled back.\n\nAlternatively, you can use the &#96;DELETE&#96; statement via the SQL proxy, like in the following example:\n\nWhen dealing with a large number of records, there is a 60-second timeout. To avoid the SQL proxy's timeout, delete in small batches.
